target.title: fix(agents): strip runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105113: runtime stream-boundary markers `[e~[` / `[e[` / `[1]` leak into user-visible channel deliveries.

When a tool-using assistant reply passes through the final channel delivery boundary, some streaming transports inject internal delimiters that the existing sanitizer pipeline does not strip — the markers reach the user as visible noise appended to the end of each message.

## Root Cause

The `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline strips `<tool_call>`, `<function_calls>`, `<system-reminder>`, MiniMax tool XML, legacy bracket blocks, and several other internal scaffolding patterns. However, it does **not** cover runtime stream-boundary markers (`[e~[`, `[e[`, `[1]`), which are functionally analogous to SSE `[DONE]`. These markers are injected at the transport layer and survive all existing strip stages.

## Fix

Add `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` to the `sanitizeUserFacingText` pipeline. The function strips:

- `[e~[` / `[e[` — stream boundary marker (SSE `[DONE]` analog)
- Trailing `[1]` — compact marker after the boundary (only at end of text)
- Trailing lone `[` after whitespace — truncated marker fragment

Inline `[1]` references ("See [1] for details") are **preserved** — only a trailing `[1]` at the very end of the text is stripped.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts` | New `stripRuntimeStreamMarkers` function + call in pipeline |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — OpenClaw main + PR patch, live Node.js import

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { sanitizeUserFacingText } from '...'; ..."

PASS: Stream boundary suffix  "Hello, how can I help?[e~[" → "Hello, how can I help?"
PASS: Variant without tilde   "Done.[e["                  → "Done."
PASS: Only marker             "[e~["                      → ""
PASS: Trailing compact marker "Done.[1]"                  → "Done."
PASS: Trailing lone bracket   "Partial reply ["           → "Partial reply"
PASS: Double-space bracket    "Done.  ["                  → "Done."
PASS: Inline reference preserved  "See [1] and [2]..."    → unchanged
PASS: Multi-line preserved    "Item [1]\nItem [2]"       → unchanged
PASS: Normal text unchanged   "Hello world"              → unchanged

✅ ALL 9 TESTS PASS
```

### Vitest

```
✓ strips runtime stream-boundary markers from user-visible text (#105113)
✓ strips compact runtime stream markers trailing the boundary (#105113)
✓ preserves inline [1] references that are not trailing stream markers
✓ removes trailing lone bracket fragments from truncated stream markers
```
